subject: Clarify SOC 2 coverage + bridge letter for Dedicated pool / audit period
messages:
From: Jordan Mills <security@acme-corp.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procure@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 scope questions — Dedicated pool + bridge letter

Hi Karthik,

We're in the final stages of Acme's security review for an upcoming purchase of Redwood Dedicated capacity. A couple of items we need clarified before legal signs off:

1) Does Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report (most recent) cover customers who use Dedicated pools (reserved GPU capacity), or is the report limited to your Hosted multitenant service? Specifically: if our workloads run in a Dedicated pool provisioned by Redwood but managed by Redwood (tenant isolation enforced at the hypervisor/container layer), will that fall under the SOC 2 scope?

2) If the dedicated pools are covered, can Redwood provide a bridge letter covering the period between the SOC 2 report end date (2026-09-30) and the close of our procurement (expected mid-April)? The bridge letter should attest no material changes to controls relevant to security and availability.

3) How do Private deployments (VPC with customer-managed networking, or on-prem packages) factor into the SOC 2 coverage? If we opt for Private later, what evidence would be available?

Requested deliverables (if available):
- SOC 2 Type II report (PDF)
- Draft/standard bridge letter for Dedicated pools
- Short statement (one paragraph) on Private/VPC applicability
- Any system description excerpt or control mapping that demonstrates tenant separation for Dedicated pools

Would appreciate a response by EOD Friday so we can include in our vendor pack.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Mills
Sr. InfoSec Analyst — Acme Corp

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SOC 2 scope questions — Dedicated pool + bridge letter

Karthik / Lauren — quick factuals and a suggested response below.

Factual clarifications (short):
- Scope: Our SOC 2 Type II (period ending 2026-09-30) covers Redwood's managed control plane and the inference runtime as operated by Redwood in the Hosted and Redwood-managed Dedicated offering. The SOC 2 system description and tests include controls around tenant isolation, access controls, change management, and patching for both Hosted and Dedicated modes when Redwood retains operational control of the infrastructure.

- Dedicated nuance: "Redwood-managed Dedicated" (customers who purchase reserved GPU pools that Redwood provisions and operates) are included in the SOC 2 scope. Customer-managed Dedicated deployments (where customer brings their own hardware or we only ship an appliance) are not covered. We should avoid the phrase "all Dedicated" — instead use "Redwood-managed Dedicated pools provisioned and operated by Redwood".

- Private/VPC/on-prem: Private deployments where the customer controls networking and physical host boundaries are out of scope for the hosted SOC 2. For VPC-hosted deployments where Redwood manages the control plane but the customer manages networking, we can provide a limited statement describing which control responsibilities remain with Redwood and which are customer responsibilities. For on-prem/air-gapped, SOC 2 evidence is generally unavailable — we can offer a controls mapping and, where applicable, a technical attestation for the components Redwood continues to operate.

Bridge letter guidance (we should provide):
- We can issue a bridge letter that: (a) references the 2026-09-30 SOC 2 report, (b) states that there were no material changes to controls related to security/availability since the report period through a specific date, and (c) limits applicability to Redwood-managed Dedicated pools and Hosted API only.
- We should not extend the bridge letter to cover customer-managed or on-prem deployments.
- Draft attachment: bridge_letter_dedicated_draft_v1.docx (I put a draft in the shared drive with legal-friendly language).

Recommended deliverables to send to Acme: 
1) Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026-09.pdf (full report)
2) system_description_excerpt.pdf (pages with the system boundary + tenant isolation)
3) bridge_letter_dedicated_draft_v1.docx (draft bridge — ask Acme if they'd like redlines)
4) short paragraph (1–2 sentences) on Private/VPC applicability (see suggested wording below)

Suggested one-paragraph wording for Private/VPC to send to customer:
"Private (VPC) deployments that use customer-managed networking and host infrastructure are not covered by Redwood's hosted SOC 2. For VPC configurations where Redwood continues to operate the control plane and inference runtime components, Redwood can provide a controls-responsibility matrix and an attestation describing which controls remain in Redwood's operational scope."

I'll include the three files in my reply draft. Note: no material control changes after 2026-09-30 that would affect security/availability controls — I checked the change log and patch records; only minor routine patching and non-product infra upgrades.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

(attachments: bridge_letter_dedicated_draft_v1.docx (draft), system_description_excerpt.pdf)
